name: Tenerife
title: Holidays in Tenerife
intro: Winter sun, a volcano with a cable car and some of Europe's best water parks. Here's what Tenerife is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Tenerife is warm all year, which makes it a favourite for winter sun and February half term. Summer is hot and busy with school holidays. The south is sunnier and drier than the green north.

things.name: Mount Teide cable car
things.blurb: Ride up Spain's highest mountain to a moonscape of old lava. Book ahead.

things.name: Siam Park
things.blurb: A Thai-themed water park often voted the best in the world.

things.name: Whale and dolphin trip
things.blurb: Pilot whales live off the south coast all year and are seen on most trips.

things.name: Loro Parque
things.blurb: A big animal park in Puerto de la Cruz, with penguins and parrots.

things.name: Playa de las Teresitas
things.blurb: A long golden beach in the north with calm water.

things.name: Teno and Masca
things.blurb: Hairpin mountain roads, cliffs and a tiny village in the north-west.

faqs.question: Is Tenerife good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's an easy, warm, four-and-a-half-hour flight, with plenty of family hotels, water parks and calm beaches.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week is typical. Hiring a car for a day or two lets you see Teide and the north.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, Tenerife is part of Spain, so British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: North or south?
faqs.answer: The south has the sunniest weather and most family resorts. The north is greener and more traditional, with more cloud.
